tip.title: Which meaning fits?
tip.text: Many English words have more than one meaning. "Bank" can be a place for money or the side of a river. "Light" can mean not heavy or not dark. To choose the right meaning, look at the sentence: What kind of word is it here (a thing, an action, a describing word)? What are the nearby words about? Swap in each meaning and keep the one that makes sense.

passage.title: The Fair at the River Bank
passage.text:
The town fair was set up on the wide bank of the river, just below the bridge. By nine in the morning the field was already crowded. Vendors had staked their stalls in neat rows, and the smell of grilled corn drifted over everything.

Joy had saved fifty pesos for the fair. It was not much, so she had to be fair with herself: one game, one snack, nothing more. At the ring-toss booth she watched a boy miss five times in a row. The rings were light, almost like paper, and the bottles were set far apart. "The game is not fair," she thought, and walked on.

At the next stall, an old man was carving small animals from wood. A tiny carabao caught her eye. "Twenty pesos," he said. She turned the carving over in her hand. The wood was smooth, and the horns were carved with real care. Joy paid, bought a cup of grilled corn with the rest, and sat on the bank to watch the river. She had spent exactly fifty pesos, and she did not regret a single one.

words.meaning: people who sell things, usually in a market or on the street
words.example: The vendors shouted the prices of their fruit.

words.meaning: fixed in place using stakes (pointed posts)
words.example: They staked the tent before the wind came.

words.meaning: to feel sorry about something you did
words.example: I regret not studying for the test.

items.prompt: "The fair was set up on the wide bank of the river." What does bank mean here?
choices: A place that keeps money
The land along the edge of a river
A row of switches
To trust someone
items.why: The sentence is about a river and a bridge, so bank means the land beside the water.

choices: The smell of grilled corn drifted over the field.
A crowded town fair was set up on the river bank, with vendors' stalls in neat rows.
The fair was just below the bridge.
Town fairs are the best part of the year.
items.why: It keeps the place, the crowd, and the stalls. Choices A and C are single details, and choice D is an opinion the text never gives.

items.prompt: "She had to be fair with herself." Which meaning of fair fits?
choices: A festival with stalls and games
Light in color
Honest and reasonable
Fine weather
items.why: Being fair with herself means being honest and reasonable about how much to spend.

items.prompt: Why did Joy decide on only one game and one snack?
choices: Her mother told her to save money.
The stalls were too far apart.
Fifty pesos was not much to spend.
She did not like grilled corn.
items.why: "Joy had saved fifty pesos for the fair. It was not much, so she had to be fair with herself: one game, one snack, nothing more."

items.prompt: "The rings were light, almost like paper." What does light mean here?
choices: Not heavy
Not dark
A lamp
To start a fire
items.why: Comparing the rings to paper tells you they weigh very little.

items.prompt: The word fair appears with THREE different meanings in the passage. Which is NOT one of them?
choices: A festival
Honest
Not cheating
Light-colored hair
items.why: The passage uses fair as a festival, as being honest with oneself, and as a game that does not cheat. Hair color never appears.

items.prompt: Why did Joy decide the ring-toss game was not fair?
choices: The boy was cheating.
The rings were too light and the bottles too far apart to win.
It cost too much.
The vendor was rude.
items.why: She noticed the light rings and far-apart bottles after watching the boy miss five times.

items.prompt: Which detail could a summary of the story LEAVE OUT?
choices: Joy had only fifty pesos to spend.
Joy decided not to play the ring-toss game.
The old man's stall was right next to the ring-toss booth.
Joy bought a wooden carabao for twenty pesos.
items.why: Where the stall stood is a small detail. The other choices are the key events that explain Joy's choices.

items.prompt: Which sentence BEST summarizes the whole story?
choices: Joy watched a boy miss five times at the ring-toss booth.
A girl went to a fair and had fun with her friends all day.
With only fifty pesos, Joy skipped an unfair game, bought a carved carabao and grilled corn, and was happy with how she spent it.
Fairs are full of games that waste your money.
items.why: Choice C covers the budget, the choices she made, and how she felt. Choice A is one scene, choice B adds friends not in the story, and choice D is an opinion.

items.prompt: What happened because Joy paid twenty pesos for the carving and used the rest on grilled corn?
choices: She had spent exactly fifty pesos.
She had to borrow money from the old man.
She went back to play the ring-toss.
She had thirty pesos left for another game.
items.why: "Joy paid, bought a cup of grilled corn with the rest... She had spent exactly fifty pesos."
